newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Gas price expectations fuel MOL rally.
newsitem.headline: Gas price expectations fuel MOL rally.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian oil firm MOL continued their rally on Friday reaching a new record high of 4,185 forints in Budapest in heavy activity and $22.25 in London, before retreating modestly, traders said.
At 1002 GMT, MOL traded in Budapest at 4,040 forints, up 110. In London MOL's Global Depositary Receipts were marked at $21.825 at 0958 GMT, up 0.9250.

"There are hot expectations of the size of the gas price increase," one trader said. "A factor of uncertainty will be dispelled as the fact that gas prices were not brought to market levels yet, left MOL shares somewhat undervalued."
Szabolcs Fazakas, minister for Industry, Trade and Tourism may decide the size of the gas price increase as early as today based on proposals by the Energy Office.
"Eliminating uncertainties will not only boost MOL's price but will improve its results as well," the trader added.

MOL's CEO Zoltan Mandoki told a news conference in late May that MOL's main burden remained the state-controlled domestic gas sale price which is causing the company's gas business to remain in the red despite legislation guaranteeing an eight percent return on equity for energy companies.
